title: Newburgh parks board begins work on 2028-2032 master plan
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Newburgh parks board begins work on 2028-2032 master plan
Deputy Town Manager Andrea Baloni said the board is still using topography and soils data that is 15 years old and hopes to get updated figures.
The Newburgh Parks and Recreation Board discussed early plans for its 2028-2032 master plan update during a meeting Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026.
THE TIMELINE Deputy Town Manager Andrea Baloni, who has worked on three master plans for the board, said public meetings on the plan could begin this year or slip to winter. "I think I said fall this year. Might be winter this year this year, but it's some I at least want to have one this year and then slowly do a couple throughout 2027," Baloni said.
LESSONS FROM PAST PLANS Baloni said earlier master plans set goals too large to finish. "The other previous master plans... were very, very large overreaching. We never accomplished those top 10," she said.
DATA AND CONNECTIVITY Baloni said she is working with someone named Drew to get updated topography and soils information, since the board has been "using the same data now for 15 years." A board member raised the possibility of a trail connection from the Rivertown Trail toward Lou Dennis and asked whether regional multimodal funding could help, noting past difficulty because "the dascese wouldn't let us get close to the church property."
Baloni said she could share an existing plan showing a proposed route and said she believed regional dollars could be available.
FUNDING CHALLENGES Baloni also described the Land and Water Conservation Fund as difficult to use quickly, saying grants cause a "huge two-year delay," and noted the town was not invited to apply for a Lilly Endowment grant because its population falls below a 5,000-person threshold.
PERSONNEL AND NEXT STEPS Baloni said master plan work has slowed because her office is focused on redoing personnel handbooks before an October deadline, but said she expects to "hit it hard" in the winter.
